strikes.name: Kharg Island military targets
strikes.network_relevance: Direct adjacency to Iran's primary oil-export terminal; CENTCOM/Trump said oil infrastructure was deliberately preserved.
strikes.evidence_basis: CENTCOM video/public statement and Reuters/AP reporting
strikes.note: CENTCOM said more than 90 military targets were struck on Kharg Island, including mine storage and missile-storage sites. Do not mark oil terminal destroyed.
strikes.impact_grade: MAJOR MILITARY STRIKE; ENERGY EXPORT INFRASTRUCTURE DELIBERATELY SPARED
strikes.purpose: Reduce mine, missile and military capacity on Iran's principal oil-export island without destroying the export terminal.
strikes.effect: CENTCOM said more than 90 military targets were struck. The strike was militarily large, but public reporting explicitly says oil infrastructure was preserved.

strikes.name: Strait of Hormuz air-defense/radar strike area
strikes.target_type: air defense / ground control / surveillance radar
strikes.network_relevance: Directly related to military control/surveillance of Hormuz; not an oil-infrastructure strike.
strikes.note: CENTCOM confirmed strikes near the Strait; exact tactical sites are intentionally not plotted.
strikes.purpose: Reduce Iranian air-defense, ground-control and surveillance coverage supporting control of the Hormuz battlespace.
strikes.effect: Destroying radar/control sites can reduce detection, targeting and coordination in that sector. It does not prove Iran lost all surveillance or sea-denial capability.

strikes.name: Bandar Abbas / port-area July strike reporting
strikes.target_type: coastal military / surveillance / drone / missile infrastructure
strikes.network_relevance: Major port and Hormuz logistics node. Public reporting does not establish that oil-handling infrastructure itself was the U.S. target.
strikes.evidence_basis: Reuters: U.S. official target categories plus Iranian reporting of local explosions
strikes.note: CENTCOM said 80+ targets were struck overall; local reports included Bandar Abbas. Keep target-category attribution separate from exact local impact claims.
strikes.impact_grade: SIGNIFICANT PRESSURE; EXACT LOCAL BDA INCOMPLETE
strikes.purpose: Pressure coastal surveillance, drone/missile and military infrastructure around the main Hormuz-facing port complex.
strikes.effect: The broader strike wave is confirmed; exact local effects were not fully reconciled, so the map does not convert target counts into destroyed assets.

strikes.name: Golestan railway bridge strike report
strikes.network_relevance: Transport-network disruption. Oil-specific function not established in reviewed reporting.
strikes.note: Iranian state media reported a U.S. strike on a railway bridge in Golestan province. Coarse province-level marker because the exact bridge was not established.
strikes.impact_grade: REPORTED TRANSPORT DISRUPTION — LOW CONFIDENCE ON PRECISE EFFECT
strikes.purpose: If accurately reported, disrupt rail movement and impose repair burden.
strikes.effect: The bridge strike was reported by Iranian state media and not independently pinned. Military or oil-specific function is not established.

strikes.name: Route-to-Mashhad bridge strikes (coarse)
strikes.network_relevance: Transport-network disruption; direct oil function not established.
strikes.note: IRGC said two bridges on the route to Mashhad were attacked. Marker is deliberately coarse because bridge identities were not publicly pinned.
strikes.impact_grade: REPORTED TRANSPORT DISRUPTION — LOW CONFIDENCE ON PRECISE EFFECT
strikes.purpose: If accurately reported, slow road movement along the Mashhad route.
strikes.effect: Exact bridge identities and military function were not independently established.

strikes.name: Bandar Khamir bridges and train station
strikes.network_relevance: Southern coastal road/rail logistics disruption near Hormuz; oil-specific use is not assumed.
strikes.evidence_basis: Reuters citing Iranian news outlets; Reuters could not immediately verify
strikes.note: Seven deaths were later reported in attacks on bridges. Keep as reported U.S. strike, not independently verified precise strike solution.
strikes.impact_grade: PROBABLE LOCAL TRANSPORT DEGRADATION; PRECISE BDA NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED
strikes.purpose: Disrupt coastal transport links near Hormuz.
strikes.effect: Three bridges and a train station were reported struck. The exact effect is based on Iranian/local reporting and was not immediately independently verified by Reuters.

strikes.name: Bandar Abbas bridges / tunnel / rail junction campaign
strikes.target_type: roads, bridges, tunnel, rail junction, communications
strikes.network_relevance: Direct logistics isolation pressure on Bandar Abbas/IRGC-port complex. Oil relevance is indirect unless a specific petroleum flow is established.
strikes.note: AP reported at least six bridges and a tunnel damaged around Bandar Abbas and a railway junction west of the city hit; a maritime communications tower was destroyed July 17.
strikes.purpose: Isolate and complicate movement around the Bandar Abbas/IRGC-port complex and degrade maritime communications.
strikes.effect: AP reported at least six bridges and a tunnel damaged, a rail junction hit, and a maritime communications tower destroyed. This is concrete network damage, but not proof the entire port or city was disabled.

strikes.name: Iranshahr Airport strike report
strikes.network_relevance: Eastern logistics node; no direct oil-network role established in reviewed reporting.
strikes.note: Reported U.S. missile attack; Reuters could not immediately verify.
strikes.purpose: Potentially disrupt an eastern logistics/aviation node.
strikes.effect: The strike was reported but not independently verified in the reviewed record; no firm operational effect should be assigned.

strikes.name: Hormozgan military logistics strike wave (coarse)
strikes.target_type: surveillance / military logistics / underground storage / maritime capability
strikes.network_relevance: Official strike category associated with Hormuz-control campaign; not a civilian oil-route marker.
strikes.note: CENTCOM confirmed the target categories but did not publicly provide exact coordinates.
strikes.impact_grade: CONFIRMED STRIKE WAVE; EFFECTS NOT FULLY PUBLIC
strikes.purpose: Attack surveillance, military logistics, underground storage and maritime capability supporting Iranian strike generation and Hormuz control.
strikes.effect: CENTCOM confirmed the target categories, but did not publish enough precise BDA to turn every target into a verified loss.

strikes.name: IRGC command/missile/drone/coastal strike wave (Iran-wide coarse)
strikes.target_type: IRGC command / missile / drone / coastal surveillance / naval
strikes.network_relevance: Iran-wide military strike wave; exact relationship to rail/oil routes depends on individual target and is not assumed.
strikes.note: CENTCOM said dozens of IRGC sites inside Iran were struck. Marker is an Iran-wide reference point, not a literal impact coordinate.
strikes.impact_grade: CONFIRMED LARGE STRIKE WAVE; LOSS TALLY UNRESOLVED
strikes.purpose: Renew attrition against IRGC command, missile, drone, coastal surveillance and naval networks.
strikes.effect: The operation is confirmed. Publicly verifiable destroyed-equipment totals remain incomplete.

strikes.name: IRIS Dena — confirmed U.S. sinking
strikes.tally: 1 frigate sunk; 87 bodies recovered; Iran later claimed 104 killed
strikes.note: Reuters and AP confirmed the U.S. submarine attack and physical recovery off Sri Lanka. This is a hard loss, not an inferred BDA count.
strikes.purpose: Eliminate an Iranian Navy frigate operating outside Iranian waters.
strikes.effect: IRIS Dena was sunk. This is a hard, independently confirmed naval loss.

strikes.name: Operation Epic Fury — cumulative U.S. claim
strikes.tally: 7,000+ targets; 6,500+ combat flights; 100+ Iranian vessels damaged/destroyed
strikes.note: Useful for scale of effort, not a verified loss count. The project ledger explicitly keeps this separate from independent BDA.
strikes.impact_grade: SCALE-OF-EFFORT CLAIM — NOT A VERIFIED LOSS TALLY
strikes.effect: The 7,000+ targets / 100+ vessels figure is an official U.S. claim. It is useful for operational scale but cannot be treated as independently confirmed destruction of 100+ vessels.

strikes.name: Bandar Abbas infrastructure degradation
strikes.tally: At least 6 bridges + 1 tunnel damaged; rail junction hit; maritime comms tower destroyed
strikes.note: This is a concrete transport/C2 effect. It does not prove the entire port or city was disabled.
strikes.purpose: Interrupt road, rail and communications supporting the Bandar Abbas military/logistics complex.
strikes.effect: At least six bridges and a tunnel were damaged; a rail junction was hit; a maritime communications tower was destroyed. The damage is real and operationally meaningful, but geographically bounded.

strikes.name: Ahvaz airport aircraft parking / runway strike
strikes.target_type: Iranian military aircraft parking area and runway at Qasem Soleimani / Ahvaz International Airport
strikes.network_relevance: Air-force sortie generation and aircraft preservation; airport-wide civilian/operational shutdown is not inferred.
strikes.evidence_basis: Existing forensic-v1.3.2 geolocation using public strike video and imagery comparison
strikes.note: Promoted from the forensic geolocation layer. The coordinate is the geolocated aircraft-parking strike point, not a whole-airport damage polygon.
strikes.purpose: Destroy parked Iranian military aircraft and degrade airfield use.
strikes.effect: Public geolocation/imagery supports destruction of F-5/F-27 aircraft at the parking area and runway cratering by March 5-6; the operational status of every airframe and the whole airport is unresolved.

bda.finding: F-5/F-27 aircraft destruction geolocated to this point; runway cratered by March 5. Operational status of every parked airframe is not established.
bda.limitations: Point is a geolocated strike/BDA reference, not a whole-airfield footprint.

strikes.name: Bandar Abbas naval base — Kilo submarine berth loss
strikes.target_type: Kilo-class submarine at Bandar Abbas naval base
strikes.network_relevance: Direct loss of Iranian subsurface naval capacity relevant to Hormuz sea denial.
strikes.evidence_basis: Planet imagery reviewed by The War Zone plus U.S. leadership statements; coordinate promoted from forensic-v1.3.2
strikes.note: The reference point identifies the submarine berth area. Imagery showed one Kilo present/untouched March 2 and assessed sunk by March 4; exact impact moment remains bounded by that window.
strikes.purpose: Reduce Iranian submarine capability supporting sea denial and threats to commercial/naval traffic.
strikes.effect: One Kilo-class submarine was assessed sunk at the Bandar Abbas berth. The record does not generalize that loss to every Iranian submarine.

bda.finding: One Kilo-class submarine visible March 2 and assessed sunk by March 4; U.S. leadership separately described a heavily damaged Iranian submarine.
bda.limitations: Commercial Planet imagery is link-only; reference point is the berth area, not a copied commercial-image damage polygon.

strikes.name: Bandar Abbas submarine / ship maintenance facility — Corsair strike
strikes.network_relevance: Directly targets Iranian naval maintenance capacity tied to attacks on commercial shipping.
strikes.evidence_basis: CENTCOM official video plus public geolocation and USNI reporting
strikes.note: Three Corsair one-way attack surface vessels struck the port. The point is a third-party geolocation of the shown facility; exact post-strike damage extent is unresolved.
strikes.purpose: Degrade submarine/ship maintenance capacity supporting Iranian attacks on commercial shipping.
strikes.effect: CENTCOM confirmed three Corsair unmanned surface vessels hit the maintenance facility and said the strike degraded Iran's ability to continue attacking commercial shipping; public footage ends before complete BDA is visible.

bda.finding: Three one-way attack surface vessels visibly impact the submarine/ship maintenance facility; exact damage extent requires post-strike imagery.
bda.limitations: Official strike video confirms impacts but is not a complete post-strike structural survey.

strikes.name: IRGC Ashura Garrison, Isfahan — imagery-confirmed damage
strikes.network_relevance: Regime-security and military infrastructure; exact strike-level U.S. versus Israeli attribution is unresolved.
strikes.evidence_basis: Bellingcat open Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 damage analysis promoted from forensic-v1.3.2
strikes.note: The coordinate is a low-confidence public-map complex reference point, not a claimed impact coordinate. The visible damage is strong; strike-level attribution remains unresolved.
strikes.impact_grade: HIGH-CONFIDENCE VISIBLE STRUCTURAL DAMAGE; ATTRIBUTION UNRESOLVED
strikes.purpose: Campaign target function assessed as military/regime infrastructure; actor-specific purpose is not assigned.
strikes.effect: Open SAR/optical imagery shows a large damage/change signature at the garrison.

bda.finding: Large damage/change signature corroborated in open optical imagery.
bda.limitations: Damage is supported; exact impact points, destroyed-component count and U.S.-versus-Israeli strike attribution are not established.

strikes.name: Fath Air Base, Karaj — imagery-confirmed damage
strikes.network_relevance: Air-force basing/support infrastructure; exact strike-level U.S. versus Israeli attribution is unresolved.
strikes.evidence_basis: Bellingcat open Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 damage analysis promoted from forensic-v1.3.2
strikes.note: Airfield reference point, not an individual impact coordinate. Bellingcat reports damage to multiple large buildings on the north side of the base.
strikes.impact_grade: HIGH-CONFIDENCE VISIBLE STRUCTURAL DAMAGE; ATTRIBUTION UNRESOLVED
strikes.purpose: Campaign target function assessed as air-base infrastructure; actor-specific purpose is not assigned.
strikes.effect: Sentinel imagery shows damage to multiple large buildings on the northern side of Fath Air Base.

bda.finding: Damage to multiple large buildings on the north side of the base.
bda.limitations: Airfield reference point is not an impact point; runway/aircraft operational status is not inferred beyond visible structural damage.

strikes.name: Khojir missile production complex — imagery-confirmed damage
strikes.network_relevance: Directly affects ballistic-missile production capacity; exact recovery time and underground inventory survival remain unresolved.
strikes.evidence_basis: Bellingcat open Sentinel analysis plus Washington Post satellite review
strikes.note: Reference point locates the Khojir complex, not a specific impact. Public imagery shows large damage clusters; later reporting assessed severe production disruption.
strikes.purpose: Degrade Iran's ballistic-missile production base; strike-level U.S. versus Israeli attribution remains unresolved.
strikes.effect: Satellite reviews documented major damage across propellant/production areas; later Washington Post analysis reported 88 structures destroyed at Khojir and assessed short- and medium-range missile production temporarily halted across the wider strike campaign.

bda.finding: Large damage clusters on eastern and western sides of Khojir near reported propellant-production areas; later satellite analysis reported 88 structures destroyed.
bda.limitations: The complex reference point is not an impact coordinate. Production disruption is substantial but does not prove permanent elimination of the missile program or destruction of all underground stockpiles.
